title: Senior Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
description:
Who We Are 

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team 

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role 

We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them.

The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production.

In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application.

Track 1: Pre-training 

This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include:

- Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run.

- Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

- Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories.

- Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data.

- Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

- Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities.

- Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods.

Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL.

Track 2: Post-training and continual learning 

This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include:

- Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO.

- Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

- Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change.

- Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions.

- Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items.

- Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments.

- Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance.

Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction.

Responsibilities across both tracks 

- Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve.

- Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online.

- Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

- Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared.

- Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions.

Minimum qualifications 

- A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

- At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation.

- Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems.

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

- Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results.

- Clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred qualifications 

- Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track.

- Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling.

- Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production.

- Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments.

What we offer 

- Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction.

- Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

- The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply 

If you want to work on these problems, we would like to hear from you. Please indicate the track and research areas that best match your experience, and include examples of work that show your contribution.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing. 

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page . 

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

title: Project Sceptrum - Multilingual AI Coding Evaluation Specialist - Dutch
description:
Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit. 

About the project 

Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result. 

About the roles 

There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets. 

- 
Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus. 

- 
Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context. 

Who we are looking for 

- 
Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English. 

- 
Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language 

- 
Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role. 

- 
Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail. 

Project at a glance 

- 
Project duration: one week since the mid of November 

- 
Languages: Dutch

- 
Project time commitment: 6 hours per person 

- 
Project compensation: varies depends on different programming language 

- 
Work location: fully remote 

How selection works (major steps) 

- 
Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability. 

- 
Language test: short exercises in the target language. 

- 
Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track. 

- 
Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role. 

- 
Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production.

Location: London, Baker Street office, four days a week (a move to Primrose Hill is likely within a couple of months). London-based candidates only. No relocation and no visa sponsorship in this hiring cycle.

Job Type: Full-time

About 36 Labs

36 Labs is an applied AI research firm in London. It works on a problem most models are still bad at: making creative decisions, and explaining why they were made. The team wants models to reason creatively, more like a person would.

Today the product is a harness that sits over any frontier model, video generation models in particular. It handles ideation, generation and distribution end to end, and the content goes out to real audiences. The results feed a data loop that keeps improving the harness. The first use case is music marketing, and the clients are the major labels, including Sony, Warner and Universal.

The company has been profitable since it started operating. It is closing its first seed round within the next couple of weeks, and the round was oversubscribed. The team is about ten people, with four engineers who report to the CTO. He is still very hands-on in the code.

You would join at a big moment. V3 of the harness is being released, which is a huge scope of work. A migration to Cloudflare is planned, and it falls mostly to the backend engineer. The stack is Python, TypeScript, Postgres, LLM and generative model APIs, and open-weight models.

What you are expected to do:

- Migrate many of the company's systems to Cloudflare. This is your first big task.

- Work on a bit of everything as needed. Engineers here are not siloed, and the structure is flat.

- Take a direction from the team and own it, without close supervision.

- Explain your approach back to the team and talk it through. Disagreement is welcome.

What you need to succeed:

Experience

- You have 4+ years of experience, including years building and running back-end systems in production. You know how they were deployed and operated.

- You are hands-on as an engineer in the AI-native era, and you keep reviewing how you work. You follow the latest stacks, models and practices.

- You have owned something real before. Ownership and leadership are visible in your CV and your projects.

How you work

- You take initiative and work independently. The culture here is high agency: it is often easier to ask for forgiveness than permission.

- You communicate clearly and can explain your ideas to the team and discuss them. No big ego.

- You are comfortable with an extremely fast pace and very little stability.

Practicalities

- You are based in London and happy to be in the office four days a week.

- You do not need visa sponsorship in this cycle. A visa that expires next June is fine.

- Nice to have: a degree in computer science, engineering, maths or stats. An MSc or PhD is a real plus. With a BSc only, your track record needs to be really strong.

- Nice to have: projects beyond your university or company roles. Where you studied matters little, and what you have built matters more.

What you get:

- Seed-stage experience that builds a wide range of skills and looks good on a CV.

- Room to move into a more senior role as the CTO gradually steps back from the code to focus on strategy.

- A company that is profitable, with an oversubscribed first round and another fundraise planned in the next nine to twelve months.

- Work with the major music labels as clients, and a rare problem: improving creativity in models. The team believes that if creativity in LLMs is solved, human attention is within reach.

- A big scope from day one: the V3 harness release and the Cloudflare migration.

- A flat team where direction is given, ownership is yours and challenge is welcome.

How to apply

Send your LinkedIn profile or CV, plus any projects you are proud of, to the recruiter who shared this role. Use the subject line "Backend Engineer – 36 Labs". We screen candidates first, then introduce a small number to the client. The process: a first conversation with Benedict, Head of Operations (CV, projects, motivation, fit), then a technical interview of about 30 minutes with the CTO, then a take-home assessment. An onsite working session happens only if needed. Timelines are quick, but a notice period of around a month is fine.

title: Engineering Lead
description:
About Doit 

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe. 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society. 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. 

The Role 

KIRA builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Engineering Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems . This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own 

- Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

- Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

- Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

- Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

- Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

- Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

- Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For 

- 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

- Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

- Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

- Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

- Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

- Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have 

- Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

- Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location 

This is a remote role . We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones. 

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Applied AI Engineer, CyberSecurity, Defense
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Role Summary

We are seeking an Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineer to build customer use cases on top of the Mistral stack for our defense, government and critical-infrastructure customers. You will turn "we have agents" into "we shipped something a client uses." This role is about composing cybersecurity-related agentic workflows focused on cyberdefense, configuring harnesses for real-world scenarios, and delivering value directly to clients — often in sovereign, on-premises or classified environments.

You will work with some of the most security-sensitive organizations in the world: government agencies, sovereign institutions and operators of critical infrastructure. They need AI that is powerful, controllable and deployable on their terms.

Why this role: 

you will build some of the first AI-for-cyberdefense systems deployed in real government and defense environments, on frontier models you can influence. You will work in a tight-knit team alongside elite experts in DFIR and cyberdefense — people who are passionate about their craft — and the patterns you implement at customer sites feed directly back into Mistral's internal use cases and products. Few roles put this much frontier technology this close to missions that matter.

What You Will Do

Client-Facing Agentic Solutions 

- You'll individually help deploy into production use cases with considerable business impact, with defense and government cybersecurity assignments as a priority

- You'll work on state-of-the-art GenAI applications, driving a crucial technological transformation together with our customers

- Tackle iconic customer use cases that no existing solution on the market can address — from custom configuration of cybersecurity harnesses for cloud defense, to agentic alert triage and investigation, incident response automation, detection engineering, threat intelligence analysis, and security log analysis at scale

- You'll be involved in pre-sales calls to understand potential customers' needs, challenges, and aspirations, providing technical guidance on our products and explaining Mistral technologies to various stakeholders

- You'll collaborate with our product and science teams to continuously improve our product and model capabilities based on customer feedback

- Ship secure by design. Apply least-privilege access, secrets management, authN/authZ best practices, audit logging, human-in-the-loop approval for high-impact actions, and defenses against prompt injection and data exfiltration in agentic systems

- Design and run evaluations that measure technical correctness, operational value and safety, so customers can trust what is being deployed

- Own deployment end to end — observability, reliability, cost and latency tuning — including on-premises and air-gapped setups where customers require them

Our Principles

- We care about people and outputs

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- No politics. Low ego, high standards

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it

Security & Compliance criteria

- Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now).

- Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance

About You

- You are fluent in French, with strong English — this customer set works in French

- You have 5+ years building systems in a cybersecurity context — SOC automation, DFIR automation, detection engineering, security tooling, or similar — with a record of operating what you ship in production

- On top of that, you have 1+ year of hands-on experience building agentic or LLM-based systems, ideally in production — with a deep understanding of the concepts: prompting and context engineering, RAG, tool use, agentic orchestration, evaluations, guardrails, and knowing when to use each. If you don't have the production year yet, deep familiarity and the drive to learn fast in real, constrained environments is what we're looking for

- You have strong technical coding skills in Python, plus full-stack experience: APIs, back-end services and front-end interfaces (e.g. TypeScript/React)

- You have strong communication skills, with an ability to explain complex technical concepts in simple terms to both technical and non-technical audiences

Ideally, you have: 

- Experience with security tooling or workflows (SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, threat intel)

- Experience as a Security Operations Engineer, Detection & Response Engineer, or Incident Response Engineer

- Experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer

- Prior work with government, defense, or national-security customers

- A bias toward action and delivery — you ship fast, operate independently with a customer-led mindset, and reuse internal building blocks effectively

- Strong problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and a collaborative attitude

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

Privacy Policy 

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

title: Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer
description:
Auterion builds a cutting-edge operating system for autonomous robotic systems that empower a diverse range of platforms to perform surveillance, reconnaissance, inspection, mapping and logistics tasks. Our industry-leading software drives the adoption of robotic fleets and is recognized by the U.S. government as the future standard for its drone programs. 

We are looking for a Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer taking on tasks within the AuterionOS ecosystem, from writing applications to adding driver support for new peripherals, maintaining system services and optimizing performance on embedded platforms. You will be working closely with:

- Linux running on embedded hardware

- C/C++, Python & Bash codebases

- Engaged and friendly engineers from across Auterion

Responsibilities 

- Work within the Board Support team and collaborate with other development teams to build leading-edge products.

- Add features, solve bugs, write tests and improve the performance of software components running on AuterionOS, Auterion’s custom embedded Linux distribution.

- Collaborate with engineering and product teams to understand both internal and customer use cases.

- Propose new software solutions and take ownership of the implementation. Your technical expertise will have a huge impact on bringing Auterion’s drone products to market.

- Provide expert support (L3) to customers facing technical issues.

- Write clear and concise internal documentation, in addition to contributing to the public-facing knowledge base.

- Participate in daily stand-ups, as well as release planning and task prioritization meetings.

Qualifications and Skills 

- B.Sc./M.Sc. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related fields.

- 3+ years of experience writing object-oriented C++ and/or Python code in a professional setting.

- Extensive experience working with embedded architectures, including cross-compilation, debugging, and performance optimization.

- Expert Linux skills, with an excellent grasp of command line operations, resource management, systems services and networking.

- Deep knowledge of the Linux kernel, embedded device drivers, device tree configuration and u-boot.

- Experience with Debian/Ubuntu-based systems, Debian packaging workflows and managing complex Docker environments.

- Knowledge of OTA updates (e.g. mender).

- Proficient in networking concepts across all layers of the OSI model, including connectors, and hardware interfaces, IP addressing, routing protocols, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, etc.

- Skilled in using network diagnostic tools (e.g., Wireshark, tcpdump) to identify and resolve network issues.

- Basic embedded security knowledge, such as secure boot on embedded devices and/or UEFI, boot chain verification.

- Proven experience with network security protocols (e.g., SSL/TLS, VPNs) and best practices for securing embedded devices, such as secure boot and encryption mechanisms.

- Basic electrical engineering experience, such as familiarity with schematics and the instrumentation required to debug communication over I2C, SPI, UART, CAN bus.

- Bonus: Experience with video streaming and MIPI CSI drivers.

- Bonus: Experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms and their associated BSP packages.

- Bonus: Experience with NXP iMX8 platforms and their associated BSP packages.

- Bonus: Previous contributions to open source projects, especially in the Linux ecosystem.

- Bonus: Experience with CI/CD systems, such as Jenkins, GitHub actions, GitLab CI.

- Experience working in an agile environment, providing daily updates in stand-ups and managing tasks in a sprint board.

- A product-oriented mindset, with an eagerness to drive forward project initiatives.

- EU Citizenship required.

Benefits 

- Flexible working hours

- Stock Options

- Generous holiday allowance

- Company pension plan 

- Car parking 

- Enhanced maternity & paternity leave

- Mental health and wellbeing support

- Learning and development opportunities

About Auterion 

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

- Support in-person activation where it matters: meetups, hackathons, community-led events and the ambassadors who host them.

Engage developers directly

- Proactively reach out to promising builders and projects to invite them into the community and our programs.

- Excellent written communication in English, with a warm, authentic and concise voice; comfortable representing a brand publicly.

- Data-driven: you define KPIs, use analytics and community tooling to assess program health, and tell the story of impact to leadership.

- Strong project and stakeholder management across Product, Engineering, Marketing and Partnerships in a fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environment.

- Passion for AI and the open-source ecosystem, with the curiosity to stay current as the field moves.

Nice to have 

- Fluency in French; other languages are a plus for regional programs.

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs (Python or TypeScript), or a public portfolio of projects on GitHub or Hugging Face.

- An existing network of developer creators, open-source maintainers or community leaders in the AI space.

- Experience with community platforms and tooling such as Discord bots, Discourse, Common Room, Orbit-style analytics or a CRM.

- Experience running hackathons, student programs or community-led meetup networks across multiple countries.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team 

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role 

Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.

This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.

In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.

In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.

What the role involves 

- Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.

- Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.

- Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.

- Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.

- Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.

- Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.

- Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.

- Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.

- Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.

Minimum qualifications 

- At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.

- Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.

- Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.

- Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.

- Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.

- Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.

Preferred qualifications 

- Experience with language-model training or post-training.

- Experience with agent or gaming environments.

- Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.

- Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.

What we offer 

- Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.

- Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.

- Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

title: AI Platform Engineer
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.

The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.

This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.

You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

- 
Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.

- 
Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.

- 
Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.

- 
Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.

- 
Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.

- 
Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

- 
Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion.

- 
Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim.

How You'll Think

Recursive Thinking

You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix.

The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which means the suite has to be right in a way the agent does not, and the thing that grades has to be graded too.

Inversion Thinking

You start from the failure and work backward to the design. The rule is that an agent may never autonomously write a commitment into a shared work system. The weak implementation is an instruction in a prompt. The strong one is that the credential in the agent's tool grant physically cannot set an owner, a due date or a status, so no amount of clever input, prompt injection or model error produces the forbidden write. You reach for the second one first.

Same for evaluation. Before writing a suite you enumerate how the agent can be wrong: an update that invents progress that did not happen, one that quotes a private channel into a public digest, one that is accurate and reads as an accusation, one that credits the wrong person. Then the suite is that list, each case caught before the agent ships rather than after it embarrasses someone.

AI-Native Execution

You use agentic tools on real work, in files and repositories, with the same rigor you apply to anything else you ship. You have a setup of your own and can describe it mechanically: what triggers it, what it is allowed to touch, where the human approves, what it logs, and how you found out the one time it went wrong.

That experience is this job, generalized. You are building for async engineers across 40+ countries who will judge the platform by whether it saves them an hour or costs them one, so you are your own first user and your own harshest reviewer.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must Have

- 
Have shipped production LLM agent systems that other people depended on. Not demos, not internal showcases. Systems with operational history, real users and at least one incident you can talk through. Prompt engineering on its own does not clear this bar.

- 
Design evaluations, not spot checks. You build golden sets, write behavioral assertions, define judge rubrics, set pass thresholds and gate CI on the result. You can explain why "we reviewed a bunch of outputs and they looked good" is not evaluation.

- 
Have done deep API work against the systems work actually lives in , and have authored MCP servers. You know the specific failure modes of those APIs, not just that they exist.

- 
Own infrastructure end to end in Python on GCP, with a cloud warehouse and infrastructure as code. You provision, deploy, monitor and roll back your own systems, and you close architecture decisions rather than routing them onward.

- 
Have taste about how software contacts humans. You treat every notification as spending a limited amount of trust.

Strong Signal

- 
Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite.

- 
LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on.

- 
You have built an internal platform that non-engineers adopted voluntarily , and can describe what you changed after watching them use it.

What Success Looks Like

- 
The platform is boring. Agents run on a schedule and on events, state survives restarts, failed runs roll back cleanly, and every run can be reconstructed from its log.

- 
Nothing ships unevaluated. Every registered agent has a real suite with safety cases, the gate blocks regressions, and when someone challenges an output the answer is a test case rather than an argument.

- 
The dangerous action is impossible, not discouraged. An audit of any agent's credentials shows it cannot perform the writes it is not allowed to perform, and the audit log makes every consequential decision traceable.

- 
Teams pull the platform instead of being pushed. Agents get adopted because the reports are useful and the contact is rare and well-timed, and each team ends up with at least one workflow that runs automatically.

- 
The platform reports its own value. The work absorbed is measured and published, so the case for expanding it is made with data rather than enthusiasm.

What We Offer 

- 
Fully Remote 

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

- 
ESOP 

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- 
Tech Allowance 

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

- 
Health Benefits 

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- 
Annual Off-Sites 

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- 
Flexible Work 

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- 
Professional Development 

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team 

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- 
~400 team members

- 
60+ countries

- 
20+ languages spoken

- 
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

The estimated base salary range for this role is $180,000-$230,000.

- 
Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

- 
Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Application Instructions

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

Interviewing with TRM 

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

Structure and solve problems

Increase speed and leverage

Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Buyer
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

The Buyer Domain at Vinted is dedicated to creating a seamless and highly engaging experience for our members as they search, discover, and purchase items. Our challenge is unique: unlike standard e-commerce, our peer-to-peer catalogue consists of hundreds of millions of entirely unique, single-inventory listings, with millions of new items uploaded daily. Connecting the right buyer with the perfect item in real-time is at the very core of Vinted's success.

The CVP team owns the core platform and services that govern how content is geofenced, balanced, and surfaced across Vinted's growing international network of markets. We build robust systems and tooling that manage cross-border visibility, enabling smooth and gradual market connections (e.g., FR-DE, BE-FR-ES) while optimising key liquidity metrics like Sell-Through Rate (STR%) and Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) by balancing the content in multiple channels.

Our team works closely with Content Visibility Management, Search, and Recommender relevance teams to accelerate product development. Currently, we are driving the automation of content visibility experimentation & analysis. Rather than having different content channels independently re-implement visibility controls, we are building a unified platform to provide autonomy to Decision Scientists. In addition, we are highly contributing in growing new large markets such as the USA and Australia.

In this position, you’ll 

- Drive technical execution: Design, implement, and maintain highly scalable, reliable, and secure backend systems to ensure efficient content visibility and search mechanisms.

- Guide technical decisions: Contribute to and challenge the technical direction of our backend services, leading system design reviews and ensuring high-quality, maintainable code.

- Scale features globally: Implement and shape A/B tested features that positively impact our 80+ million users. Code changes are rolled out instantly to production.

- Own your services: Monitor and improve backend service performance and stability. The team owns and monitors service-layer measurements (SLIs, SLOs, etc.) and has an on-call rotation which you will participate in.

- Lead team-level initiatives: Lead and drive technical initiatives within the team, while collaborating on domain-wide integrations with other engineering teams (such as Search and Recommender relevance teams).

- Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with engineering and product managers, analysts, and other stakeholders, facilitating clear communication within the team and across domains.

- Contribute to product direction: Provide technical feasibility assessments, identify technical risks, and provide effort estimations to help shape our team's product roadmap.

- Foster engineering excellence: Mentor, guide, and share knowledge with other engineers in the team to support their technical growth and promote collaborative best practices

About you 

- You have extensive experience in backend software engineering, with a proven track record of designing and building scalable, distributed, and highly available systems.

- You are highly proficient in backend development. We primarily use Go, Kotlin, Ruby, Python — while prior experience in these specific languages is beneficial, a strong foundation in modern backend engineering and a willingness to learn is what matters most.

- Experience with event streaming platforms like Kafka, Apache Flink, or others for real-time data processing and message queueing.

- A track record working with search engines, information retrieval and ranking optimisations technologies (e.g., Vespa, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch) is a high advantage. If not, we expect you to have a strong willingness and motivation to learn.

- You are enthusiastic about AI technologies, use AI tools daily in your work, and proactively learn and experiment with how to adopt AI to boost engineering outcomes.

- Strong understanding of continuous integration and deployment pipelines, with experience in tools like Jenkins for automating builds and deployments.

- Experience with observability and monitoring tools (we use Grafana, Kibana, and others) to keep services healthy and define SLIs/SLOs.

- Experience working with relational and in-memory databases.

- Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience working with cross-functional peers (Product, Analytics, SRE).

- Experience in mentoring other engineers, providing constructive feedback, and promoting engineering best practices within your team.

- Excellent written and spoken English.

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- A daily lunch allowance

- Company bike leasing scheme

- Monthly budget for a flexible benefits platform

- Work from Home allowance

- Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan

- A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted

- An NS mobility card

- A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy 

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity 

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

The annual gross salary range for this position excluding 8% holiday pay is:

€76.800 — €104.000 EUR

Bridge research and engineering: Transition statistical and machine learning prototypes from initial experimentation into scalable, production-ready Python applications.

DS & ML research rigor: Proven experience in data science and machine learning research, encompassing statistics, hypothesis testing, model training, evaluation, backtesting, tuning, and model selection.

Engineering practices & communication: Confidence working with Git, code reviews, and Agile methodologies, supported by strong written and spoken English.

Cloud platforms: Experience deploying ML workloads on AWS or GCP using Docker and Kubernetes.

Workflow orchestration: Familiarity with orchestration tools such as Apache Airflow, Kubeflow, or MLflow.

Streaming technologies: Exposure to real-time streaming architectures (e.g., Apache Kafka).

You will help us build new capabilities and features in our product suite, including things we haven’t yet imagined possible, and you will drive those changes forward into our customers’ hands.

About you 

You are an enthusiastic generalist who thrives in the face of ambiguous requirements—an engineer who is just as good at starting things as you are at finishing them. Some qualities we value most:

High agency 

You are driven. When something important feels daunting or underspecified, your first instinct is to prototype to clarify the value you can deliver, rather than wait for someone to give you the answers.

Boldness in learning 

You are genuinely unafraid to tackle unfamiliar subjects. You know that nobody is an expert in everything, and you don't let unfamiliarity be a reason for not trying. You're not afraid to ask questions and make mistakes, because learning new techniques feels like an adventure and we share what we learn as a team. Proficiency in either Go or Typescript as well as in either Python or R, and experience with backend systems, data tooling, and data science frameworks are helpful for this role. Eagerness and boldness to learn is essential. 

User empathy and product sense 

You make judgment calls on behalf of users with minimal up front guidance and are willing to be wrong, because you will learn. Prior domain expertise with data science as a practice may help, but it is not the only way. Regardless, you lead with empathy: you optimize for solving a real customer problem, not for technical purity.

Collaborative curiosity 

You are generous. When you learn something useful, your first instinct is to share it. You teach as readily as you learn, ask questions without ego, admit what you don't know, and lend a hand when someone's stuck.

Interest in AI 

You are interested not just in using AI in your work, but building tools for customers to use AI in their own work. You also are curious, and you question when AI is not the right answer for a particular problem. You lean on your user empathy when building: knowing that some of our customers use and love AI in data science and others don’t or are restricted from using it.

Results-driven 

You are focused on delivering measurable value to customers. You have a strong technical background with a track record of shipping successful products. 

Within one week, you will… 

- Ship code changes that meaningfully improves the experience for our customers.

Within one month, you will… 

- See your changes reflected in our public releases.

- Participate in feature planning and provide feedback.

- Feel comfortable navigating the codebase and understand how things fit together.

Within three months, you will… 

- Plan features and drive their development.

- Have a track record of teaching team members; both from your expertise and things you learn as you build. 

- Have a track record of learning: both from the things you learned and taught us along the way; and from listening to internal users, external users, and how our customers use our products.

Within six months, you will… 

- Point to new features you built that we hadn’t even dreamed were possible.

title: Ubuntu Linux Kernel Test Engineer
description:
Ubuntu is the most widely used Linux distribution in the world, delivering kernels across a vast matrix of versions, architectures, and configurations – with up to 15 years of security and maintenance commitments for Long Term Support (LTS) releases. Ensuring the quality and reliability of these kernels demands a dedicated, systematic approach to testing at scale.

The Canonical Kernel Team is looking for a Test Engineer to take ownership of our kernel testing strategy and infrastructure. You will design and maintain test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security. You will build and evolve automated test frameworks – including stress testing, fuzzing, code coverage analysis, and regression detection – that not only must remain effective across many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance, but must be able to scale with the high demand for Ubuntu kernels (currently more than 160 under active support).

The successful candidate will bring strong Python skills, familiarity with Linux kernel internals, and experience building test infrastructure that scales. You will work closely with kernel engineers to catch regressions early, validate fixes, and ensure every kernel we ship meets the highest standards of reliability.

Location: This role will be based remotely in the APAC region, except for Taipei, Taiwan, and Beijing, China, which are office-based locations.

What your day will look like

- Design, develop, and maintain comprehensive test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security for Ubuntu Linux kernels

- Build and improve automated test infrastructure for continuous kernel quality validation across multiple kernel versions and architectures

- Maintain long-lived test suites that evolve alongside Ubuntu’s many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance

- Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for continuous kernel quality validation

- Conduct performance benchmarking and regression detection across kernel releases

- Measure and improve kernel code coverage, identifying gaps in test coverage and creating tests to address them

- Execute and analyze stress tests covering CPU scheduling, memory management, I/O subsystems, networking, and filesystem workloads

- Develop and maintain fuzzing harnesses to discover kernel vulnerabilities and reliability issues using tools such as syzkaller, Trinity, or custom fuzzers

- Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team

- Contribute to upstream test suites and testing frameworks

- Document test methodologies, results, and coverage gaps

What we are looking for in you

- Significant programming experience in Python

- Experience with test frameworks such as LTP, kselftest, xfstests, stress-ng, fio, or similar

- Experience designing and executing system-level tests: functional, stress, performance, or regression testing

- Familiarity with CI/CD systems (Jenkins, GitHub CI, or similar)

- Experience maintaining test suites over long periods, adapting to evolving software across multiple supported versions

- Familiarity with Linux (Ubuntu or Debian preferred but not required), Linux kernel internals and subsystems

- Experience with Linux systems administration and automation

- Solid background with git

- Well-organized, self-starting and able to deliver to fixed schedules

- Professional written and spoken English with excellent communication skills

- Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each

Additional skills that you might also bring

- Familiarity with kernel fuzzing tools and techniques (e.g. syzkaller, Trinity, AFL, or custom harnesses)

- Experience with code coverage instrumentation (e.g. gcov, kcov, LLVM source-based coverage)

- Knowledge of kernel tracing and observability tools (e.g. ftrace, perf, bpftrace, eBPF)

- Familiarity with static analysis tools (e.g. sparse, smatch, Coccinelle) as part of a testing workflow

- Experience with fault injection frameworks (e.g. failslab, fail_make_request) for reliability testing

- Prior experience with test infrastructure at scale (provisioning, orchestration, result aggregation)

- Experience with Ubuntu/Debian packaging or Snap

- Knowledge of virtualization technologies (KVM, QEMU) and container runtimes

- Cloud infrastructure experience (AWS, GCP, Azure, or OpenStack)

- Prior involvement with open source testing communities or projects

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce. 

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

- Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!

- Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum

- Annual compensation review

- Recognition rewards

- Annual holiday leave

- Parental Leave

- Employee Assistance Programme

- Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’

- Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical 

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer 

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
