title: Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations
description:
At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We deliver user-friendly corporate applications, manage complex data ecosystems, and provide efficient tech solutions across the organization. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover.

We’re hiring a Engineering Lead to build the systems that help our clinical teams deliver services in the field and in members’ homes. You will own technical direction and delivery for scheduling, dispatch, field and mobile workflows, and the software that connects equipment and home technology to the operation.

A likely first assignment is an “Air Traffic Control” system for field operations. A supervisor needs to understand what is happening and act when the plan breaks: a flat tire, a delayed visit, a missing piece of equipment, or a member whose availability changes. You will work with the people doing the job to decide what they need to see, what the system can help resolve, and when a human should intervene.

This is a hands-on role that spans product and engineering. You will understand the business problem, shape the solution, build useful increments, and see whether they work. You may start without direct reports and can expect to coach and eventually manage one or two engineers. You should enjoy building personally and helping others become more capable.

We value a tinkering instinct: try the unfamiliar tool, inspect the data, trace the failure, put a small improvement in front of a user, and learn from what happens. Hardware or connected-device experience can be a strong signal of that mindset, but it is not required. The central work is building dependable software for an operation that changes throughout the day.

As an Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations, you will: 

- Work directly with supervisors, clinical field staff, and operations leaders to understand schedules, travel, capacity, handoffs, and the exceptions that disrupt a day’s work.

- Build field visibility and intervention tools that give supervisors useful context, distinguish current facts from missing information, and help them respond to changing conditions.

- Develop scheduling and dispatch capabilities that match people and visits to practical constraints, with clear ways for operating staff to review and adjust the plan.

- Build and debug APIs, mobile workflows, integrations, and data flows supporting field teams, connected equipment, and home technology.

- Prototype quickly and ship focused increments. Make deliberate choices about what to build, integrate, or buy, and avoid committing to a large system before the operation has tested the approach.

- Use AI actively for development, investigation, prototypes, analysis, and useful workflow capabilities. Check the behavior and make failures understandable and recoverable.

- Coach engineers and take on a small number of direct reports as the team develops. Maintain clear ownership, sound engineering practices, and credible delivery commitments.

- Partner with Product, Special Project Leads, IT, Counterpart, and the Engagement lead at the interfaces their work shares with field operations.

Success in this role looks like: 

- First 90 days: You understand how the field operation works, have shipped an improvement used by supervisors or field staff, and can show what it changed. You have a focused technical plan grounded in real constraints and exceptions.

- First six months: Several useful increments are in place. Supervisors can understand and respond to disruptions more effectively, scheduling and field workflows are improving, and technical ownership is clear.

You should get in touch if: 

- You are a strong production software engineer who has owned meaningful work end-to-end and still builds regularly.

- You can move across backend services, APIs, data flows, user interfaces, and operational workflows to solve a real problem.

- You have strong product instincts, learn unfamiliar domains directly, and enjoy working with the people using what you build.

- You have an iterative, curious approach to technology. You can describe an unfamiliar system you explored, a practical prototype you tried, or a failure you traced across boundaries.

- You use AI in your own engineering work and have practical experience building or integrating AI-backed capabilities, with clear verification and evaluation.

- You can coach engineers and are interested in responsibility for a small team as it develops. Formal management experience can help, but a strong record of Engineering Leadership and coaching also matters.

Benefits Overview : 

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

title: Research Engineer - Cybersecurity (RL Environments)
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

Cybersecurity is one of the areas where AI could do the most good — and one where the capability must be built with particular care. As a Research Engineer on this track, you'll push our models' capabilities in vulnerability discovery and remediation, security analysis, incident response , and across the offensive-to-defensive spectrum of cybersecurity, and it will be your job to develop that ability deliberately and safely.

The work sits at the meeting point of research and engineering: you'll devise new approaches and be the one to implement them. Concretely, that means designing and building RL environments that reproduce realistic security scenarios, pipelines that generate synthetic training instances at scale , and experiments and evaluations that show what our models can actually do. Your results feed directly into the production training runs that shape our frontier models, in close collaboration with Mistral's researchers, engineers, and security specialists.

Security specialists and ML engineers are both welcome here — what matters is that you can hold your own in both worlds, and are eager to go deeper on the one you know less.

What You Will Do

- Design and implement RL environments simulating cybersecurity scenarios.

- Build the pipelines and infrastructure that generate synthetic cybersecurity training instances at scale — thousands of scenarios, not one hand-crafted exercise.

- Conduct experiments and evaluations of model capabilities on these environments, from quick prototypes to controlled benchmark runs.

- Own the infrastructure behind the environments: containers, sandboxes, VMs, cloud deployments, and orchestration (Kubernetes) , all managed as code.

- Partner with researchers and security specialists across Mistral, distilling their domain expertise into reproducible environments and datasets.

- Write clear, efficient code in Python and enforce strong software-design practices: testing, code review, CI/CD.

What We're Looking For

- Hands-on expertise in offensive and/or defensive cybersecurity : vulnerability analysis, web/network/cloud security, secure coding practices, and SOC.

- Strong software engineering skills : clean, reliable, well-tested code — not just exploit scripts.

- Fluency in Python plus comfort reading lower-level languages (C/C++) for vulnerability analysis.

- DevOps experience : Docker, Kubernetes, cloud deployments, sandboxed or simulated environments.

- A pragmatic research-to-engineering mindset: ship a working first version, then refine and scale it.

- Working knowledge of RL techniques and LLM training methodologies , or strong motivation to develop it.

- Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative — comfortable working across research and engineering.

Nice-to-haves

- CTF, cyber-range, or bug-bounty experience — as a player, challenge author, or platform builder.

- A research background in cybersecurity, academic or industrial, or in another experimental discipline.

- Prior experience building RL environments or large-scale ML training infrastructure.

- Relevant open-source contributions and projects.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. title: Principal Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
description:
Who We Are 

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced applied scientist to help set LCM’s research direction and work directly on its most demanding scientific problems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role in a flat team of around 30 engineers, with no direct reports. You will mentor colleagues and contribute to hiring, but you will not manage people.

We define how a capability will be evaluated before developing it, and use that evidence to guide training and deployment decisions. You will help decide which research questions deserve investment, design and run experiments, and develop training methods that can be used across applications.

The role requires deep expertise in a core area of model training and the judgment to connect that work with decisions about data, evaluation and deployment. Scientists and engineers work together from the first experiment through to production evaluation, and you will take scientific responsibility for agreed research projects.

A central research goal is to learn from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio and turn useful signals into regular updates to model weights.

What the role involves

- Develop the research agenda with the team, identifying questions that affect model quality, training efficiency or downstream results. Use experiments to decide which approaches warrant larger training runs and which should be revised or stopped.

- Lead selected research projects through implementation, training and evaluation, staying directly involved in writing code, inspecting data, debugging runs and analysing failures.

- Establish evaluation methods that separate real improvements from leakage, noise and benchmark overfitting, and work with portfolio teams to test whether offline gains hold in controlled online experiments.

- Mentor scientists and engineers through joint research, experiment reviews and technical discussion, and advise on work that crosses project boundaries.

- Contribute to hiring, publish research and support the release of models, benchmarks and training methods where the work and data can be shared.

Research areas

The initial focus will depend on your expertise and the team’s priorities. We expect substantial depth in one of the two areas below, with the ability to contribute to decisions across the other.

Pre-training and representations 

We continue pre-training open-weight models on commerce data. Research questions include how to represent users and catalogues, how to combine data from different businesses, and how to allocate compute effectively. Work may include:

- Studying data mixtures, scaling behaviour and training schedules to guide the next run.

- Designing sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, including alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

- Developing mid-training methods for capability acquisition, context extension and retention of general capabilities.

- Evaluating synthetic data and distillation methods through controlled experiments, including the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

- Studying transfer across languages, markets and commerce categories, with evaluations for new users and items and for performance on future data.

- Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation, including pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data.

Post-training and continual learning 

We train LCM for commerce tasks and a range of agent applications, including customer-facing assistants and agents that carry out business operations. We also develop continual learning methods that turn new interactions into regular updates to model weights. Work may include:

- Developing supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning methods, using verifiable outcomes or learned reward models.

- Turning session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback into training examples and rewards, accounting for exposure bias, delayed feedback and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

- Studying data selection, replay and update frequency so models learn from new interactions without losing established capabilities.

- Training and evaluating decision models that choose rankings, offers and promotions, using offline learning and off-policy evaluation to estimate policy value and uncertainty and inform controlled online experiments.

- Training models for multi-turn conversations and multi-step agent workflows, including understanding user intent, planning, tool use, maintaining context, recovering from errors and verifying outcomes. This includes building RL environments with simulated users and catalogues, and testing whether gains transfer to real interactions within defined permissions and business rules.

- Calibrating reward models and LLM-based graders against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and investigating reward hacking and other unintended effects.

- Developing automated experimentation methods that propose and test changes to training recipes, prompts, tools or agent control flow, with held-out evaluations and regression checks.

How we evaluate the work

Research should produce evidence that supports a training or deployment decision. We use strong baselines, including existing production systems, and weigh model quality against compute requirements, inference cost and latency.

Experiments should be reproducible, with ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis. They must account for temporal leakage, changes in the data distribution and differences between companies and markets. Negative results are valuable when they explain a limitation or stop further investment in an approach that does not work.

The work also involves data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories, together with our data and engineering teams.

In the first three months, we expect you to establish a focused research programme, resolve an important training or evaluation question, and work with the relevant teams to test the resulting method in a downstream application.

Minimum qualifications

- A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

- At least eight years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with at least four years leading research directions that were published or reached production.

- Substantial experience developing and training models, with deep expertise in pre-training, post-training or reinforcement learning relevant to the areas above.

- A record of original contributions, shown through research papers, released models, benchmarks, open-source projects or significant advances in deployed systems.

- Scientific leadership: choosing research directions, resolving difficult technical questions and helping experienced colleagues make better decisions.

- Sound experimental and statistical judgment, including examples where the evidence changed your approach and the ability to recognise when the evidence does not support a conclusion.

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to work independently in a shared research codebase. Research on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

- Clear communication and a collaborative approach to disagreement, review and mentoring.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs, continual learning, synthetic data, distillation or tabular foundation models.

- Familiarity with commerce data and online experimentation.

- We do not expect expertise in every area.

What we offer

- Influence over LCM’s research agenda and which questions the team invests in.

- Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

- The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

Please include examples of research or deployed work that show your contribution, the decisions involved and the evidence used to evaluate the results, and indicate which research area best matches your depth.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing. 

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page . 

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

Want to know more about life at Prosus? Explore our culture and values .

title: Principal Software Engineer - Observability & Telemetry Data
description:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Observability Engineering owns the breadth and depth of observability and telemetry at Smartsheet. We build and operate the shared platform every engineering team depends on to understand how their software behaves in production (metrics, logs, distributed traces, RUM, synthetics, and AI/agentic telemetry) across a global, multi-region, commercial and government footprint. We are consolidating ownership of all of it into a single correlated platform, and treating telemetry as what it actually is: one of the largest and most valuable datasets at the company. It's a broad mandate with real scope to shape, and we hold this internal platform to the same rigor, reliability, and product standards as customer-facing software. 

As a Principal Software Engineer (Observability & Telemetry Data) , you will set the technical direction for how Smartsheet collects, models, stores, and derives value from telemetry data. This is an architect role: you will define the telemetry data platform and the standards that govern it, carry that architecture across engineering org boundaries, partner with our Data and AI Platform teams on Databricks and MLflow integration, and act as the company's definitive technical voice on observability. You will influence roadmaps you do not own, resolve the hard design trade-offs between fidelity and cost, and raise the technical bar for every engineer instrumenting a service. 

This full-time position reports to the Team Lead, Observability Engineering and can be located in our Bellevue, WA office, or you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer. 

You Will 

- Architect the Telemetry Data Platform: Own the end-to-end design for how telemetry is landed, modeled, and queried, including open table formats, partitioning and schema evolution strategy, separation of storage and compute, tiered retention, and the query interfaces engineers actually use. Make telemetry a durable, portable, Smartsheet-owned dataset rather than a vendor-locked byproduct. 

- Own the Telemetry Data Model: Define the semantic conventions, shared business identifiers (user, org, plan, tenant), and schema standards that let any signal be correlated with any other, and drive their adoption across every service team at Smartsheet. 

- Set OpenTelemetry Direction: Lead the migration to OTel-based instrumentation, defining collector architecture, context propagation, and sampling strategy (including tail-based sampling) so that engineers can move from a log line to a trace to a metric without losing the thread.

- Integrate AI and Agentic Telemetry with Databricks: Own the architecture connecting our observability platform to Databricks and MLflow, so that agentic and model telemetry (prompt, completion, tool and MCP calls, evaluation results) is captured un-sampled, stays useful under the input/output redaction our governance requires, and reconciles cleanly with the traces and metrics in our primary observability stack. 

- Instrument the Data Platform Itself: Bring first-class observability to our data estate, including Databricks jobs, pipelines, and warehouses, with meaningful signals for freshness, data quality, lineage, and cost, so data reliability is measured with the same discipline as service reliability. 

- Build the Analytics Layer on Telemetry: Turn telemetry into decision-grade analytics, covering reliability and incident metrics, telemetry cost and chargeback models, and adoption and coverage reporting that leadership can act on. 

- Engineer Collection and Routing at Scale: Architect the high-volume collection and routing tier (FluentBit, Kinesis, and OTel collectors) that moves telemetry from every service to its destination across US, EU, AU, and GovCloud regions, and own the migration of these pipelines as we consolidate onto a unified backend. 

- Own Telemetry Economics: Set the cost architecture for observability data, including ingest governance, cardinality control, and storage tiering, so that teams get the fidelity they need to debug without the spend pressure that causes them to under-instrument. 

- Carry Architecture Across Org Boundaries: Partner with the Data Platform, AI Platform, and infrastructure organizations to align telemetry architecture with theirs, influence roadmaps you do not own, and represent observability in company-level platform and vendor decisions. 

- Raise the Technical Bar: Lead design and code reviews, author the architecture decisions and standards others build against, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers on instrumentation, telemetry data modeling, and cost-aware design. 

- Participate in a production support and on-call rotation, taking ownership of the most complex issue resolution and driving root-cause analysis that improves system resiliency. 

You Have 

- 10+ years of experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, data platforms, or observability infrastructure, including time at Principal or Staff level. 

- Deep Observability Expertise: Hands-on production ownership of metrics, logs, and distributed tracing at scale, including at least one major backend (Datadog, or comparable) and a working understanding of cardinality and cost mechanics. 

- Telemetry Data Engineering: Demonstrated depth in large-scale data architecture, including open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg), Spark or comparable distributed processing, streaming ingestion, partitioning and schema evolution, and query performance and cost tuning over very large datasets. 

- Databricks Depth: Practical experience with the Databricks platform (jobs, clusters, Unity Catalog, Delta) and with MLflow for model and agent telemetry. 

- OpenTelemetry Depth: Practical experience with OTel collectors, semantic conventions, context propagation, and sampling strategy, including tail-based sampling. 

- Pipeline Engineering: Experience with high-volume log and telemetry pipelines, including FluentBit or Fluentd, streaming transport such as Kinesis or Kafka, and search backend index and mapping design.

- Advanced AWS & Kubernetes Expertise: EKS, ECS Fargate, EC2, Lambda, and CloudWatch in production. 

- 10+ years of programming experience with modern languages such as Go, Java, Python, or Scala, and strong SQL. 

- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, and GitOps workflows such as Flux or ArgoCD. 

- Architectural Influence at Scale: A track record of setting technical direction that multiple teams and organizations adopted, including the written artifacts (architecture decisions, standards, RFCs) that made it durable after you moved on. 

- Strong incident response instincts, with experience improving mean-time-to-resolution through better instrumentation and better data rather than more heroics. 

- A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical industry experience.

- Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis 

Nice to Have 

- Experience instrumenting LLM or agentic systems, including OTel GenAI semantic conventions and tracing agent tool-call workflows. 

- Data reliability engineering practice: freshness, quality, and lineage SLOs for production data pipelines

- Telemetry cost engineering or FinOps at scale. 

- Experience in regulated environments (FedRAMP, GovCloud) and designing telemetry that remains useful under redaction. 

- Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager. 

- Snowflake, or experience operating across more than one lakehouse or warehouse platform. 

- Service catalog or internal developer platform work (Backstage or similar). 

Current US Perks & Benefits: 

- Employer subsidized medical/vision and dental coverage for full-time employees

- 401k Match to help you save for your future (50% of your contribution up to the first 6% of your eligible pay)

- Monthly stipend to support your work and productivity

- Flexible Time Away Program, plus Sick Time Off

- US employees are automatically covered under Smartsheet-sponsored life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability plans

- US employees receive 12 paid holidays per year

- Up to 24 weeks of Parental Leave

- Personal paid Volunteer Day to support our community

- Opportunities for professional growth and development including access to Udemy online courses

- Company Funded Perks, including a counseling membership, local retail discounts, and your own personal Smartsheet account

- Teleworking options from any registered location in the U.S. (role specific)

Smartsheet provides a competitive base salary range for roles that may be hired in different geographic areas we are licensed to operate our business from. Actual compensation is determined by several factors including, but not limited to, level of professional, educational experience, skills, and specific candidate location. In addition, this role will be eligible for a market competitive incentive opportunity. 

US Base Salary Pay Range

$222,500—$257,500 USD

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/vertican-senior-applied-ai-engineer-document-intelligence

title: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.

This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.

As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: 

- Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.

- Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. 

- Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.

- Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.

- Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.

Success in this role looks like: 

- In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.

- By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.

- By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.

You should get in touch if: 

- Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.

- You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work. 

- Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Bonus points if: 

- 

- You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.

- You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.

- You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.

- You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.

Benefits Overview :

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society. 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. 

The Role 

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Technical Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems . This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

- Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

- Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

- Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

- Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

- Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

- Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

- Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For 

- 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

- Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

- Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

- Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

- Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

- Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have 

- Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

- Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location 

This is a hybrid role . You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week , with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Verticals (AI Native)
description:
Headquarters: Canada

URL: http://www.life360.com 

About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries. 

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com .

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

This role sits on the Verticals team within Life360 — the group building the next frontier of meaningful connection beyond the core family circle. This role's initial focus is Aging in Place: helping aging parents stay safely independent while giving the families around them real peace of mind. Over time, this role may flex to support other emerging verticals — Things (Tile, connected trackers) or Pets — as priorities shift, so we're looking for someone who wants to help define the pattern for new member segments, not just ship one feature set.

We are a product-minded, AI-Native engineering team. That means AI isn't just a tool we use — it's how we work. We've redesigned our team workflows around AI, treating it as a first-class collaborator at every stage: ideation, coding, testing, review, and iteration. We ship faster and go deeper because of it, and we're looking for someone who wants to help define what that looks like at scale.

About the Job

Life360 is hiring an AI Native Senior Software Engineer — a senior engineer who doesn't just use AI tools, but thinks natively in them. You'll be central to how the Verticals team builds products.

You'll design and build features that serve one of our most important and fastest-growing member segments: aging parents who want to stay safely connected with, and independent from, the families who care about them. As priorities change, you may also apply these same patterns to Things (connected trackers) or Pets.

You will take full ownership of what you build from the first line of code through production, on-call, and the member impact it has. You obsess over the humans on the other end of the product, not just the ticket.

Full-stack experience is required for this role — you should be comfortable moving between backend services and the mobile surfaces that expose them. Our stack spans Spring Boot microservices, Java, Kafka, and Kafka Streams on the backend, a modern cloud-native platform on AWS, and native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps on the client side.

In your first year, success looks like having shipped end-to-end features serving the Aging in Place member segment and establishing at least one AI-native workflow the broader team adopts.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $103,500 to $192,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 149,500 to 177,500 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers. 

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) , as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits. 

What You’ll Do

- Ship end-to-end across the stack — from backend services and APIs through to the iOS and Android surfaces members use, serving tens of millions of users — moving between layers as the feature demands.

- Work with AI (Claude Code) as a first-class collaborator — orchestrate agents to create specs, generate code, and perform reviews, moving faster without sacrificing quality.

- Define and codify AI-Native engineering practices for the Verticals team, establishing playbooks the broader org can adopt.

- Collaborate closely with product managers and designers to turn complex user problems into scalable engineering solutions.

- Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and a culture of craft and continuous improvement.

- Participate in on-call rotation and incident response.

- Mentor team members and contribute to team processes and technical standards.

- Support performance, reliability, and accessibility across the features you own.

- Adapt patterns and services built for Aging in Place to future verticals (Things, Pets) as team scope expands.

What We’re Looking For

- 4+ years of experience building and operating high-quality, consumer-scale services.

- 1+ years of hands-on experience prompting, evaluating, and building with LLMs.

- Full-stack proficiency spanning backend services (Java, Spring Boot, Kafka) and mobile client development (Swift for iOS and/or Kotlin for Android), with the versatility to work across the whole stack as needed.

- Hands-on experience with agentic workflows, prompt engineering, context window management, and MCP/function calling.

- A track record of using AI tooling to multiply your own output — not just as autocomplete, but as a development partner.

- A strong sense of ownership — you don't wait to be told what to fix, and you follow through past "it works on my machine" to "it works for the member, in production, at scale."

- Strong communication and collaboration skills — you work well with product, design, and platform engineers.

- Excitement for defining what it means to be AI-Native — you're not waiting for the playbook, you want to write it.

- Empathy for the humans behind the product — an aging parent trying to stay independent, or a family member trying to help from afar.

- Bachelor's Degree in a Technical field, or equivalent experience.

Nice-to-Have 

- Experience with IoT, telematics, or embedded/hardware-adjacent systems.

- Familiarity with Kafka, Kinesis, or other high-throughput streaming platforms.

- Background with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, DataDog).

AI-Native Expectations

We use AI coding tools as a professional standard on this team. Here's what that means in practice:

- Daily use: You use AI coding assistants (we support Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for real, substantive tasks: analysis, coding, refactoring, testing, navigating codebases, and documentation. Not just research or autocomplete but as a development partner.

- Judgment and ownership: AI-generated code gets the same review you'd give any PR. You are accountable for everything you ship.

- Velocity: We expect senior engineers who use AI well to operate with meaningful leverage — doing more with the same time, taking on problems that would otherwise require a larger team.

- Team leadership: You share what works. You automate prompting strategies that others can build on and help teammates earlier in their AI workflow adoption get up to speed.

- Continuous learning: The tooling is changing fast. You stay current and bring recommendations to the team when something would meaningfully improve how we work.

Our Benefits

- Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

- 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

- Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference 

- Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust. 

- Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

Our Commitment to Belonging

title: Compiler Engineer - Algorithmic Workloads Compilation
description:
About us 

Mythic is building the future of AI computing with breakthrough analog technology that delivers 100× the performance of traditional digital systems at the same power and cost. This unlocks bigger, more capable models and faster, more responsive applications—whether in edge devices like drones, robotics, and sensors, or in cloud and data center environments. Our technology powers everything from large language models and CNNs to advanced signal processing, and is engineered to operate from –40 °C to +125 °C, making it ideal for industrial, automotive, aerospace, and defense.

We’ve raised over $100M from world-class investors including Softbank, Threshold Ventures, Lux Capital, and DCVC, and secured multi-million-dollar customer contracts across multiple markets.

About the role 

Help push the boundaries of what can run on our accelerator. You’ll design compiler IRs and lowering strategies to support algorithmic workloads with irregular or dynamic control flow—loops, branches, and iterative methods—going beyond static neural networks. Working side by side with hardware engineers, you’ll influence ISA and execution model co-design to unlock new algorithm classes on analog and digital subsystems. The result: a compiler that makes complex algorithms practical to deploy while staying seamless for developers.

Here's what you will do

- Extend compiler IRs to represent algorithms not easily captured in DNN graphs including control flow and iterative computation

- Develop compilation strategies that unify analog compute with digital subsystems while maintaining performance and correctness

- Prototype and optimize algorithms with irregular or dynamic control flow in compiler IRs, applying techniques such as vectorization, predication, and scheduling

- Collaborate with hardware engineers to co-design ISA and features that improve support for algorithmic workloads

- Define a roadmap for higher-level programming abstractions that simplify prototyping and accelerate deployment

Here's the background we hope you will have

title: Staff Economist, Marketplace Economics
description:
Change the way the world travels 

Join the GetYourGuide journey to connect people with unforgettable travel experiences around the world. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours. 

Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step.

Team mission 

Marketplace Economics is a new team at GetYourGuide, built to answer the questions that determine how our marketplace grows and how it should be designed. How much revenue does the next euro of paid search actually return? Which marketing channels are genuinely incremental, and which are taking credit for demand we already had? What price should a supplier set, what does a change in commission do to supply, demand, and liquidity, and how should our ranking and supplier incentives be structured in the first place?

We are a senior team working directly with leadership across Marketing, Pricing, and Supply, among others, and the decisions we inform are among the largest the company makes. On the causal inference side, we draw on tools like experimental design, natural and quasi-experiments, double machine learning, synthetic controls, and more to inform marketing attribution and incrementality, spend allocation, and price elasticity. Our structural work models demand, supply, and the mechanisms connecting them, so we can reason about equilibrium outcomes and simulate counterfactuals we can't run as experiments. Most of our hardest problems in pricing and market design need both.

Your mission 

You'll be a technical lead for pricing and supply and a core contributor to our marketplace measurement work. Reporting to the Director of Marketplace Economics, you will:

- Own the economics of pricing end to end: estimate travel demand and willingness to pay, build the structural models that turn those estimates into defensible price recommendations for our supply partners, and run the experiments that validate them.

- Work collaboratively with other economists on paid marketing optimization problems across channels and geographies and funnel stages.

- Work on the design of the marketplace itself; commission and incentive structures, inventory coverage, supply liquidity.

- Partner closely with business leads in Marketing, Pricing, and Supply by translating ambiguous commercial questions into reasonable identification strategies that drive meaningful business outcomes.

- Set the technical bar for empirical rigor at GetYourGuide: raise the quality of experiment design across teams, mentor analysts and data scientists.

Your toolkit 

- PhD in Economics, or a closely related quantitative discipline with a strong applied focus.

- 5+ years of applied work after your PhD, including 2+ years at a marketplace or platform company.

title: Harness Research Engineer | 36labs
description:
Role: Harness Research Engineer

Company: 36 Labs 

Location: London, in the office four days a week (Baker Street now, moving to Primrose Hill within a couple of months). London-based candidates only. No visa sponsorship is available at the moment.

Job Type: Full-time

About 36 Labs

36 Labs is an applied AI research firm in London. It is teaching models what captures human attention on social media, and it starts with creativity. The founders see a creative process as a tree of decisions. LLMs are poor at that, and they are poor at explaining why a creative choice was made.

The product is a harness that sits over any frontier model, especially video generation models. An autonomous marketing service runs on it, from ideation to generation to distribution. The content goes to real audiences, and the results feed a data loop that improves the harness. Clients so far are mainly music companies, including Sony, Warner and Universal. Marketing is a proof of concept. The company does not see itself as a marketing business.

The company is profitable and is closing its first seed round in the next couple of weeks. V3 of the harness is being released internally, and the scope of work is large. The founders are sure of the direction. They need someone to own delivery. Today only one or two people can work on the harness, so you would be one of the first. This is a new role, created by the next stage of growth.

The stack is Python, TypeScript, Postgres, LLM and generative model APIs, and open-weight models.

What you are expected to do:

- Continue developing the harness, including the V3 release.

- Take ownership of delivering the harness. The direction is set, and getting it built is your job.

- Build and run benchmarks and evals.

- Own the evaluation pipeline for the harness, across text, video and images.

- Turn fuzzy quality questions into validated evaluation models for open-ended agent tasks.

What you need to succeed:

Experience

- You have 4+ years of experience and have owned something before, from start to finish.

- You are a hands-on engineer in the AI-native era and can work independently.

- Agents and evals are the company's main priorities. You have shipped evals for outputs that cannot be tracked automatically, such as open-ended, non-numerical tasks.

- Ideally you have shipped an agent system with real users and workloads. It relies on models, calls tools and acts on the results of planning steps. A basic chat interface with retrieval behind it is not enough, and neither is agent work limited to data extraction.

- You can work from the London office four days a week and do not need visa sponsorship right now. A visa valid until next June, for example, is fine. A month's notice is fine too. Starting earlier is preferred, though November or December is acceptable.

Nice to have

- A degree in computer science, engineering, maths, stats or similar. An MSc or PhD is great. With a BSc only, you need to be really good. The university matters less than what you have built.

- Experience with multimodal models or post-training.

- A background in applied generative media or creative companies, such as Fal.

- Projects beyond university or your day job, and a habit of keeping up with new stacks, models and practices.

How you work

- You have high agency. You take the lead and need little hand-holding.

- You do things first and ask forgiveness later, and you are open to being disagreed with.

- You explain your ideas clearly to the team and leave your ego at the door.

What you get:

- Real ownership. You would own the delivery of the harness, which only one or two colleagues can work on today.

- Work on a problem few other companies are tackling. The team believes that solving creativity in LLMs would solve the human attention economy, and they see a very high ceiling.

- Clients such as Sony, Warner and Universal.

- Fast learning at a seed-stage company, which is also a strong line on a CV.

- Room to grow into a more senior role. The CTO is expected to step back from the code over the long term.

- A pace that is extremely fast and comes without stability. The team sees that as a good thing, and we want you to know it upfront.

How to apply

Send your LinkedIn profile or CV, with a short note on the projects you are proudest of, to your contact at the agency. Use the subject line "Harness Research Engineer, 36 Labs". The process starts with a short pre-screen call with the agency. Next comes a conversation with Benedict, head of operations, then a technical interview of about 30 minutes with the CTO, then a take-home assessment. If the team is torn between strong candidates, there may be a final session on-site in the office.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you own our customer deployments end to end. Our system runs on-prem at industrial facilities, critical infrastructure, and military sites, integrated with the cameras, networks, and robots already in place. You survey the site, plan the deployment, install and integrate the system, tune it to the site's conditions, and hand it over to operators who will rely on it daily.

You are also the technical face of Laelaps on site. You work with security operators to understand how they actually work and where the bottlenecks are, align with their leadership on what success looks like, and translate what you learn into configuration, code, and product priorities. Early deployments you run alongside the founders; over time you own sites and accounts independently.

Expect roughly half your time at customer sites in Switzerland and Europe, and the rest in Zurich, turning field lessons into tooling and automation that make each deployment faster than the last. This is an engineering role with a customer in the room, not a support or services role.

What You'll Work On

- Deployments end-to-end: site surveys, network and hardware planning, installation, camera and VMS integration, commissioning, validation, and handover.

- On-prem infrastructure: install and manage our stack on edge hardware (NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson Thor class devices) inside customer networks, often air-gapped or heavily restricted.

- Integrations: connect existing cameras, sensors, VMS platforms, and robots into one coordinated system, and write the glue code where no integration exists yet.

- System tuning: calibrate detection and tracking to each site's terrain, lighting, and threat profile until the system performs in the field as it does in the demo.

- Pilots to production: make POCs succeed technically, because pilots that work become contracts.

- Customer understanding: sit with operators, interview stakeholders from the control room to the leadership floor, and map the real problems and bottlenecks behind the stated requirements.

- Customer trust: train operators, respond fast when something breaks, and be the engineer customers ask for by name.

- The deployment playbook: turn every hard-won lesson into runbooks, tooling, and automation that compound.

- Product feedback: bring real field signal back to the core engineering team and shape the roadmap with it.

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for an engineer who runs toward the messy parts, with the EQ to match the IQ. You are as comfortable in a server room or on a windswept perimeter as you are in a terminal, and just as comfortable in a conversation. You can spend a shift with a security operator and earn enough trust that they tell you what actually goes wrong at 3 a.m., then brief a head of security or a site director in their language, not yours. You listen more than you pitch, you read the room, and you switch registers between the guard house and the boardroom without breaking stride. You debug across the whole stack without ceremony: is it the hardware, the network, the driver, the model, or the config? Above all, you take personal ownership of the outcome: the deployment works because you made it work, and the customer trusts us because you earned it.

Your Background

- 3+ years of relevant software, robotics, embedded systems, or systems integration experience.

- A Master’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Strong Python and hands-on C++ experience. You can read, debug, and extend production code in both.

- Experience deploying and operating software on-prem or at the edge (Docker required; GPU inference experience a strong plus).

- Experience working with sensors and embedded systems, including device interfaces and communications protocols.

- High EQ and experience working directly with end users or customers: you can uncover needs, work across stakeholders, and communicate technical issues clearly.

- Composure in customer-facing technical sessions, including when systems fail and plans need to change.

- Fluent German and/or French, and good English. Our sites and their operators run in German; the team runs in English.

- Willingness to travel regularly to customer sites across Switzerland and Europe, with multi-day on-site stints.

- Based in or willing to relocate to Zurich.

- Citizenship of Switzerland, an EU/EFTA member state, or a NATO member state, and eligibility for security clearance where customer sites require it.

- A valid category B driving license.

Nice to Have

- Real networking competence: VLANs, firewalls, routing, VPNs, and debugging connectivity in networks you do not control.

- Hands-on comfort with hardware: you have racked servers, flashed devices, crimped a cable, or built systems that touch the physical world. Checking cable connections at 2 a.m. at a client site is second nature while debugging an issue on a customer side.

- Experience with cameras, VMS platforms (Milestone, Genetec, or similar), ONVIF/RTSP, or the physical security industry.

- Computer vision or ML deployment experience, especially optimising inference on edge GPUs.

- Robotics experience: ROS2 and Rviz2, robot integration, or fleet operations.

- Experience in defence, government, or other regulated environments.

- French, Italian, or another European language.

- Startup experience, ideally somewhere you were handed a hard problem and a deadline instead of a spec.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.
